summary: End-to-end tested the new Reconciliation Debug card on admin dashboard. Backend pytest suite (8 tests) passed 100%. Frontend admin view renders correctly with drift detected; non-admin (sales) correctly hides card with no console errors. Backend delete-orphan flow validated: deletes a real orphan, refuses on non-orphan, returns error for missing txn, blocks non-admin. One small orphan was deleted as instructed (orphan_count went 142 → 141, orphan_total decreased by exactly deleted amount). Live preview DB now shows: aggregation_total=₹9,15,76,985 (155 txns), loop_total=₹8,85,560 (14 txns), difference=₹9,06,91,425, orphan_count=141 — verdict='orphans', drift fully explained by orphans.
critical_code_review_comments: dashboard/routes.py:217 loads ALL payment_transactions into memory via to_list(100000). With 155 txns today this is fine, but if the collection ever crosses ~50k rows the endpoint will OOM. Consider a $lookup aggregation against customers + computing the orphan partition server-side instead of a Python loop.

Both /reconciliation and /reconciliation/delete-orphan return 200 with {error: ...} on auth failure instead of proper 401/403. This is internally consistent with the rest of the codebase's posture but is non-standard REST. Frontend correctly treats the error envelope as 'hide card', so functional impact is zero — flagging for future API hygiene.

ReconciliationCard.jsx:102 surfaces e?.response?.data?.detail in the error toast, but the backend returns {error: ...} (not {detail: ...}). On a real delete failure the user will see the generic 'Failed to delete orphan' fallback instead of the backend's actual reason. Low priority since the only known failure mode (customer-still-exists) is impossible to trigger from this UI (the row is by definition an orphan).

delete-orphan endpoint is non-idempotent and not audit-logged. A re-click after toast would 404, but there is no activity_log entry recording who deleted which orphan. Worth adding for compliance — financial mutations should always be logged.

Frontend silently swallows ALL errors (including network failures) via setData({unauthorised: true}) — admin will see no card if their session expires mid-fetch and won't know why. Consider distinguishing 'unauthorised' from 'fetch error' so transient failures don't hide the widget permanently until reload.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (admin render, sales gating, expand, refresh all verified; delete UI verified via API contract & visible trash buttons)

seed_data_creation: None. Per agent_to_agent_context_note, deleted exactly ONE small orphan (smallest in orphan_samples) during pytest run. Orphan count went 142 → 141. No other data mutated.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reconciliation feature works end-to-end. Backend test file at /app/backend/tests/test_reconciliation.py covers all role/data flows. DB now has 141 orphans (was 142 before my run). The 'verdict=ok' state was not reproduced against live DB (would require deleting all 141 orphans) — that branch is unit-trivial and a mock fixture can be added later if strictness is required. Frontend trash-delete flow was NOT triggered from UI (only via API in pytest) to honour the 'delete only ONE' constraint — the trash buttons and confirm dialog wiring are present and verified by code inspection, and the underlying endpoint they call is fully tested.
rca of the issue: N/A — feature addition, not a bug. The card correctly explains the existing data drift: 141 orphan transactions totalling ₹9,06,91,425 reference customer_ids absent from the customers collection, causing the aggregate-sum card (Total Revenue Collected ₹9.16 Cr) to exceed the per-customer-loop card (Total Collected ₹8.86 L) by exactly that amount.
